In pursuance to the said judgment of this Tribunal dated 07.04.2022, the appellant filed IA No.15 of 2022 in original petition no.1002 of 2010 before the Commission seeking directions to the 2[nd] respondent GUVNL to pay the amount worked out by the appellant up to April, 2022 as per the calculation sheet and the summary of the claims annexed to the application. The appellant had claimed an amount of Rs.1556 crores which included Delayed Payment Charge to the tune of Rs.1296.33 crores. The said application was disposed of by the Commission vide order dated 05.05.2023 which has been impugned in this appeal. The Commission has referred to the Article 5.3.4 of the PPA and also placed reliance upon its previous order dated 27.12.2019 in petition no.972 of 2009 filed by GUVNL against appellant and has computed the DPC amount on the bank rate and on simple interest basis. 7. Essar Power_ , 2025 INSC 1160) understood this Tribunal’s finding in the same manner; 21. In this context, it would be gainful to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in _PPN Power_ . The relevant clause therein (Article 10.6 of the PPA, as quoted in the underlying Commission judgment) provided as under: 22. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in interpreting the above clause, held at paragraph 75: **(VII) The Judgment Dated 21.03.2025 in Appeal No. 138/2021 Does - - Not Constitute a Binding Finding on Article 5.3.4 Vis a vis the Appellant** 33. We have carefully perused the Judgment dated 21.03.2025 passed in Appeal No. 138/2021 and, having considered its scope, context and operative findings, are of the opinion that it does not constitute a binding or conclusive determination of the question now before us. Our reasons are as under: (b) In that judgment, at paragraph 72, this Tribunal recorded GUVNL's submission " _that as per settled principle of law ordinarily courts are not supposed to grant interest on interest, except where it has been specifically provided under the statute or where there is specific stipulation to that effect under the terms and conditions of_ _35._ Furthermore, this Tribunal's Review Order dated 17.07.2025 in R.P. 9/2025, which was filed by Appellant seeking clarification that the Judgment dated 21.03.2025 would not affect its rights in the present appeal, is dispositive of this argument. In that order, this Tribunal specifically held: _“Since the Petitioner herein is not aggrieved by the directions passed by us in Appeal No. 138 of 2021 dated 21.03.2025 whereby simple interest was granted to the Appellant therein, the question_ 36. This observation unambiguously confirms that the question whether the PPA stipulates simple or compound interest was not decided in the Judgment dated 21.03.2025 and remains open for adjudication in the present appeal. GUVNL's submission that the earlier Judgment constitutes a binding finding on Article 5.3.4 is therefore directly contradicted by this Tribunal's own subsequent order, which was passed on EPOL's Review Petition specifically seeking this clarification. to, nor did it ever interpret Article 5.3.4 of the PPA. It is also significant that GUVNL's own written submissions before the Supreme Court drew attention to this Tribunal's Review Order dated 17.07.2025 in R.P. 9/2025, which clarified the scope of the earlier observations as academic. We reject the attempt by GUVNL to use a factual narration as a finding by the Hon’ble Supreme Court when the record clearly shows otherwise. 55. The Appeal is accordingly allowed in the above terms. All pending Interlocutory Applications, if any, stand disposed of in terms of this order.
